question: In a Google SWE interview round the candidate was asked to create a directory structure (a file-system-like tree) and handle multiple edge cases. The interviewer discussed edge cases for about 15 minutes, then the candidate coded a medium-to-hard tree solution; the interviewer then added more edge cases and a follow-up, and asked about time and space complexity and why a given data structure was used.
lookingFor: Clarifying the API and edge cases before coding
Modelling a hierarchy as a tree with children keyed by name
Correct path parsing and handling of conflicts and invalid input
Complexity and justification of data-structure choices
Extending the design when new requirements arrive
followUps: How would you implement move and prevent moving a directory into its own subtree?
How would you support wildcard search (find *.txt)?
How would you maintain directory sizes efficiently?
How would you add symbolic links without creating infinite loops?
